title: Control Plane Rule Contracts - Fastnotes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures compact, actionable notes for a rule contract/schema for the control plane routing rules (JSON/YAML flavors), the validator requirements, and a pragmatic rollout sequence (canary gating, telemetry checks, automated rollback hooks). Not a polished spec — quick reference and decisions/ops expectations.

High-level goals (keep these visible):
- Expressive but constrained rule schema so non-opinionated policies don't cause combinatorial explosion.
- Validator must be fast, deterministic, and provide clear error messages for authors.
- Rollout must be reversible with automated health gates and minimal blast radius (region-aware, capacity-tier-aware).
- Telemetry must tie directly to rollout gating: latency, error-rate, model-fallbacks, QOS drop.

Open questions (TODO):
- How much of the runtime feature semantics must be encoded in the schema vs. left to control-plane code? e.g. "fallback_priority" semantics vs enum.
- Do we require explicit model-variant compatibility flags per rule or infer via catalog?
- Canary sizing: percentage vs fixed token budget? Need experiment.

Authoring constraints (notes to SDs and SREs):
- Keep routing rules small: prefer many small rules over one huge rule blob. Rule precedence must be deterministic: first-match wins with explicit priority int.
- Avoid regex in path matching except in vetted libraries. Prefer prefix/suffix and param patterns.
- Metadata fields must be limited to keys in the schema (no freeform metadata without a schema extension).

Example JSON Schema (author-facing, minimal):
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id","match","action","safety"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {"type":"string", "pattern":"^[a-z0-9\\-]{3,60}$"},
    "priority": {"type":"integer", "minimum":0, "maximum":1000},
    "match": {
      "type":"object",
      "properties": {
        "path": {"type":"string"},
        "method": {"type":"string", "enum":["ANY","POST","GET"]},
        "headers": {"type":"object", "additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}},
        "region": {"type":"string"},
        "customer_tier": {"type":"string", "enum":["free","standard","enterprise"]}
      },
      "additionalProperties": false
    },
    "action": {
      "type":"object",
      "properties": {
        "route_to": {"type":"string"},
        "model_variant": {"type":"string"},
        "fallback": {"type":"string"},
        "weighting": {"type":"object", "additionalProperties":{"type":"number"}}
      },
      "required":["route_to"],
      "additionalProperties": false
    },
    "safety": {
      "type":"object",
      "properties": {
        "canary": {"type":"boolean"},
        "canary_policy": {"type":"object"},
        "max_p95_latency_ms": {"type":"number"},
        "max_inference_error_rate": {"type":"number"},
        "rollback_on": {"type":"array", "items":{"type":"string"}}
      },
      "required":["canary"],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}

Validator expectations (implementation checklist):
- Fast syntactic check (JSON/YAML parse) -> structural schema validation -> semantic checks.
- Semantic checks include: model_variant exists in catalog; region is supported for chosen route; weighting sums to 1.0 when present; no circular fallback chains.
- Linter provides: severity: error/warn/info and actionable messages with example fixes.
- Validator should expose a machine-readable error code (e.g. RP-101 invalid-match-path).

Runtime semantic checks (control plane runtime):
- When deploying a rule, runtime re-validates against live config: capacity availability, known model binaries, hardware constraints (GPU vs CPU), and quantization flags.
- If runtime finds an unmet constraint, it should either reject promotion or mark rule as "staged:blocked" with root cause.

Rollout mechanics (proposed short sequence):
1) Author creates rule in draft namespace.
2) CI runs static validator + unit tests (simulate routing).
3) Promotion to "canary" environment: deploy to dedicated canary pools in 1 region. Canary policy options: percentage-based (default 5%) OR token-budget-based (default 10k tokens).
4) Canary monitoring window: 30m to 2h depending on traffic. Collect metrics: p95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost delta, model fallback rate, error classification (safety failures).
5) Automated gate evaluation: thresholds (p95 delta < +15% AND 5xx delta < +0.5% AND fallback_rate < 1%) OR manual approval.
6) Gradual regional expansion (region-by-region): each step increases percent or token budget by factor of 2 with monitoring windows.
7) Promote to global after all regions pass.
8) Full rollout includes golden-sample prompts evaluation (push eval set through new route to check semantic regressions).
9) Rollback: automated if gate fails twice OR manual rollback. Rollback must be immediate and route traffic back to last-known-good route variant.

Canary telemetry signals (must be implemented in console and runtime):
- Latency deltas (p50/p95/p99) vs baseline route.
- Error deltas (5xx, 4xx spikes) and model-specific failure modes (model OOM, decoding error).
- Quality regressions: embedding similarity drop, hallucination rate on a curated prompt set.
- Cost deltas: token spend per 1k requests.
- Fallbacks: count and percentage of requests that hit fallback_action.

Automation and runbooks (ops):
- Gate evaluator is a lambda that reads metrics from telemetry, computes rolling window comparisons, emits PASS/FAIL and a structured report.
- If FAIL: first action = cut canary traffic to 0% (atomic change), then auto-create incident with template prefilled (region, rule id, last 5 minutes graphs).
- Runbook for engineers: expected steps: investigate model logs, check catalog for variant compatibility, examine capacity reservations.

Testing matrix for validator (minimal):
- Unit: schema conformance tests, error messages stable across versions.
- Integration: validator + catalog lookup using a staging catalog.
- Fuzz: random rule generation with limits to ensure validator doesn't hang.
- Performance: validate 10k rules in < 2s (goal).

Access control notes: 
- Authoring permission required: route-write. Promotion to canary requires route-promote. Only SRE and release-automation roles can bypass gating (emergency).
- Audit logs: every promotion must write a signed audit event with user, commit id, and validator signature.

Examples (short):
- Simple prefix route -> route to model-a:
{
  "id": "srv-user-login-v1",
  "priority": 100,
  "match": {"path": "/v1/auth/login", "method": "POST", "region": "us-west1"},
  "action": {"route_to": "model-pool-1", "model_variant": "m-03"},
  "safety": {"canary": true, "max_p95_latency_ms": 600, "rollback_on": ["p95_spike","5xx_increase"]}
}

- Weighted split with fallback:
{
  "id": "chat-beta-split",
  "priority": 40,
  "match": {"path": "/v1/chat", "method": "POST", "customer_tier": "standard"},
  "action": {"weighting": {"model-a": 0.9, "model-b": 0.1}, "fallback": "model-a"},
  "safety": {"canary": true, "canary_policy": {"type":"percent","initial":5}, "max_inference_error_rate": 0.01}
}

Ops heuristics / anti-patterns observed from prior rollouts:
- Too-large canary percentages (>=20%) frequently caused noisy results; prefer token-budget gating for models with bursty traffic.
- Mixing many match predicates in a single rule makes root-cause analysis much harder.
- Silent fallback definitions (no observability) lead to hidden cost increases; ensure fallback emits structured telemetry.

Back-compat and migrations:
- Schema v1 -> v2 migration must include automated migration tooling that emits a dry-run report. Backfill policy: keep old rules as-is until migration window closed.
- Validator should support a compat flag to allow temporary permissive checks for paused migrations.

Notes to implementer (quick):
- Provide a validator library (go/python) and a CLI that returns JSON errors with codes.
- Integrate with existing config-lint CI job.
- Hook audit events to KMS-signed commits for enterprise traceability.
- Make rollout engine idempotent: re-applying a staged canary should be a no-op if identical timestamped commit.

References and tickets:
- PLATFORM-987 gating telemetry dashboard (confluence)
- PLATCFG-112 schema evolution RFC draft

Last-minute checklist before promoting to public doc:
- Add explicit model_variant compatibility matrix to catalog integration docs.
- Nail down canary sizing experiment and record results.
- Add example error codes mapping for common author mistakes.

End of fastnotes.

(If you're reading this quickly: please ping in #platform-routing and add any early feedback; I will fold into the formal spec after two review cycles.)
